task_description.overview: Test if the variation of the seismic b-value over a one-dimensional parameter (e.g., time) is statistically significant.
steps: Load earthquake magnitude data and the corresponding x_variable (e.g., times).
Set or compute magnitude of completeness (mc) as a constant or vector.
Choose sliding window size n_m (15 ≤ n_m ≤ n/15) for equal-number magnitude subsets.
Select a b-value estimation method (e.g., BPositiveBValueEstimator).
Apply b_significant_1D with inputs: magnitudes, mc, magnitude increment (delta_m), x_variable, n_m, and chosen method.
Obtain output p-value, mean autocorrelation (mac), expected autocorrelation (mu_mac), and standard deviation (std_mac).
Compare p-value to significance threshold (e.g., 0.05) to decide if b-value variation is significant.

input_data.mc: float or array, magnitude of completeness (e.g. 1)
input_data.x_variable: array, parameter for ordering magnitudes (e.g., times)
input_data.n_m: int, number of magnitudes per sliding window (e.g. 100)
input_data.method: BPositiveBValueEstimator or similar estimator class (e.g. BPositiveBValueEstimator)

task_definition.agent_prompt: Using `seismostats` library to perform 1D b-value significance test. Load the catalog from catalog_path, and bin the magnitude with given `delta_m`. Then, get the `magnitude` and `time` from events, and calculate `b_significant_1D(mags, mc, delta_m, times, n_m, x_variable=times, method= BPositiveBValueEstimator)`. Output the p-value, mean autocorrelation, expected autocorrelation, and its standard deviation. Finally, use the `plot_b_series_constant_nm(mags, delta_m, mc, times, n_m=n_m, x_variable=times, color='red', plot_technique='right', label='b-positive', ax=ax, method=BPositiveBValueEstimator)` from `seismostats.plots` to plot the b-value series with constant n_m. Save the result to {result_data.save_name} with content {result_data.content} and the figure to {result_figure}.
